summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with a history of endometriosis, bipolar disorder, and chronic pelvic pain was admitted for acute-on-chronic left lower quadrant pain, similar to a recent flare one week prior. She presented with severe pain and nausea, unresponsive to home medications, and was found to have mild hypokalemia and normocytic anemia. A transvaginal ultrasound showed no acute abnormalities. Pain was managed with continued home medications, including gabapentin, tizanidine, tramadol, and lidocaine patch. Her potassium normalized, pain improved, and she was discharged home in stable condition after approximately 12 hours with follow-up scheduled with her OB/GYN and outpatient plans to evaluate her anemia.
